name: Accessory Drive
description: Water pump, 6-rib accessory belt, tensioner, idlers, alternator mount, A/C (or delete) and the 8-rib supercharger belt drive.

components.name: Mechanical water pump & gaskets
components.description: Belt-driven engine coolant pump on the front of the block feeding both heads (reverse-flow cooling). Water pump gaskets are part of the GM-style cam install kit. Some race builds replace it with an electric pump (engine-support) to free power and control temps at idle in the pits.
components.location: Front of engine on the front cover/block, driven by the 6-rib accessory belt (approximate position).

factory.name: GM Gen V LT4 water pump

raceOptions.name: Electric water pump conversion
raceOptions.notes: Requires block-off/adapter for Gen V; part numbers not verified here.

hardware.notes: Michigan Motorsports: water pump to block 18 ft-lb; Summit lists water pump bolts 89 in-lb - likely the smaller housing/cover bolts. Confirm which is which with GM service information. Checked 2026-10: Michigan Motorsports lists water pump to block at 18 ft-lb. The GM SI fastener table for the C7 LT1 (screenshots reposted on CorvetteForum) lists only water pump impeller bolts and water inlet housing bolts (10 N·m), and the TightTorque table compiled from the 2016-2018 Camaro service manual lists 'water pump fastener' at 10 N·m in two passes. Value unchanged, but confirm the thread size on your pump: if every pump fastener is M6, use 89 in-lb (10 N·m).

hardware.item: Water pump impeller housing / cover bolt
hardware.notes: Checked 2026-10: GM SI fastener table for the C7 LT1 (screenshots reposted on CorvetteForum) lists 'Water Pump Impeller Bolts 10 N·m (88 lb in)'. Rated R and Summit also give 89 in-lb.

installNotes: New gaskets; torque evenly; spin pump by hand after install.
inspection: Check weep hole for coolant and bearing play each event.

sources.title: Michigan Motorsports: LS / LT Engine Torque Specs (2014+ Gen V LT section)
Summit Racing Help Center: Chevrolet LT Gen. 5 LT1/LT2 Torque Specs
Michigan Motorsports: Gen V cam install kit for wet sump LT engines

components.name: Accessory (serpentine) belt - 6-rib
components.description: Main 6-rib belt from the crank balancer driving the water pump, alternator and A/C (if retained), kept tight by the automatic tensioner. Race cars often delete the A/C and shorten the belt.
components.location: Front of the engine (approximate routing - verify on your bracket set).

factory.name: GM 6-rib accessory belt
factory.notes: Length depends on A/C and pulley sizes.

installNotes: Measure new length with a string after any pulley/A-C change.
Check alignment of all pulleys with a straightedge.
inspection: Check for glazing, chunking, rib cracks; replace every season.

components.name: Accessory belt tensioner
components.description: Spring-loaded automatic tensioner with pulley. Weak tensioners cause belt flutter at high rpm; check arm movement while running.
components.location: Front of engine on the accessory bracket (approximate).

hardware.torque: M10 x 1.5 x 105 tensioner bolt (GM 11588754): 43 ft-lb (58 N·m); M8 x 1.25 x 45 tensioner bolt (GM 11610074): 16 ft-lb (22 N·m)
hardware.notes: Typical M10 accessory fastener value; verify with GM service information. Checked 2026-10: Chevrolet Performance LT4 wet-sump FEAD instructions 19371521/19371522 sheet 5 step 3 and LT1 FEAD 19417547 step 3 both give the M10 bolt at 58 N·m and the M8 bolt at 22 N·m. CORRECTED from a 37 ft-lb (50 N·m) estimate.

installNotes: Index the tensioner locating pin; check arm range marks with belt installed.

components.location: Front of engine on accessory brackets (approximate).

hardware.notes: Checked 2026-10: Chevrolet Performance LT4 FEAD instructions 19371522 sheet 8 step 8 give the upper and lower idler pulleys (12665845 / 12642705) at 58 N·m (43 lb-ft). CORRECTED from a 37 ft-lb estimate.

components.name: Alternator & mounting bracket
components.description: Alternator on the engine accessory bracket, driven by the 6-rib belt. The alternator unit itself is an electrical item; this component covers the mount, bolts and pulley alignment.
components.location: Front of engine, upper corner of accessory drive (approximate).

raceOptions.name: Lightweight race alternator
raceOptions.notes: Match pulley offset and charging output to ECU/PDM loads.

hardware.notes: Checked 2026-10: Chevrolet Performance LT4 FEAD 19371522 sheet 5 step 2 and LT1 FEAD 19417547 step 2 give the generator to bracket bolts (11588754, M10x1.5x105) at 58 N·m (43 lb-ft). The 2016-18 Camaro SM (via TightTorque) agrees for the LT1. CORRECTED from a 37 ft-lb estimate. The generator bracket to block M8 bolts are separate: 22 N·m per the LT1 sheet, 25 N·m per the A/C kit sheet. The LT4 sheet says 50 N·m for that bracket step, which matches the C7 SI 'generator bracket bolts 50 N·m'; check the bolt size.

components.name: Supercharger drive belt (8-rib) with tensioner & idlers
components.description: Separate 8-rib belt from the front groove of the balancer to the blower pulley, with its own tensioner and idlers. Pulley size sets boost; Harrop lists 8PK2170 for an 85 mm pulley and 8PK2145 for 70-80 mm pulleys on Camaro/CTS-V. Belt slip under sustained high rpm is a common LT4 road-race issue.
components.location: Front of engine, outermost belt plane, from crank up to the supercharger snout.

raceOptions.name: Aftermarket 10-rib supercharger drive
raceOptions.notes: Harrop offers 10PK pulleys 65-90 mm (99-PLY16390..16395-GT) for 10-rib drives.

hardware.torque: SC belt tensioner (12663624) bolts, 3x M8 (11610074): 18 ft-lb (25 N·m); SC idler pulley (12678515): 43 ft-lb (58 N·m); SC tensioner bracket (12667164): 11588730 bolts 18 ft-lb (25 N·m), 11588753 bolts 43 ft-lb (58 N·m)
hardware.notes: Checked 2026-10: Chevrolet Performance LT4 FEAD 19371522 sheets 6-7, steps 5-7. CORRECTED from a 37 ft-lb blanket estimate: the tensioner bolts are M8 at 25 N·m, not M10.

installNotes: Align SC pulley with crank groove; verify tensioner arm in range.
Recalibrate if pulley size changes (boost/MAF/airflow model).
inspection: Check for belt glazing/slip marks and tensioner bearing play every event.
